description: Remove every remaining decimal hour rendering from the user-facing worklog payloads, so an hour quantity always reads as a clock duration ('32h 15min') and never as '32,25h'. The user reported this on the work item peek view after the previous change only converted part of the surfaces: the totals cards were converted, the equivalent-hours readings, the client-facing section, the allowance ledger and the dashboards were not, and the /preview endpoint sends no display twin at all so the form prints the raw '1.2500'. Independent of FEAT-003 (this one is API + payload wiring, that one is layout), but both must land before the change is reviewable as a whole.
steps: Read .kiro/steering/worklog-contexto.md rules R3 and R11 and docs/worklog/CONVENCOES-DE-TRABALHO.md first. R11 is a hard constraint: no change here may add logged_hours, raw_duration_minutes, applied_multiplier or any rate to a client-facing payload. The change is about how an hour is RENDERED, never about which hour a role receives.

In apps/api/plane/utils/service_log_time.py, make format_hours_human able to render a value that is not a whole number of minutes without falling back to decimal notation: append a seconds tail when a remainder exists, e.g. Decimal('1.8750') (112min 30s) -> '1h 52min 30s', Decimal('0.3750') -> '22min 30s'. Whole-minute values must keep their current output exactly ('1h 15min', '45min', '30h', '0min', negatives prefixed with '-'), because the existing assertions in apps/api/plane/tests/unit/utils/test_service_log_time.py::TestFormatHoursHuman all use whole-minute inputs and must keep passing unchanged. Round to the nearest whole second (ROUND_HALF_UP) as the last resort for a sub-second remainder, and document in the docstring why that is safe: logged hours are multiples of 0.25 and multipliers have two decimal places, so every real product is a multiple of 0.0025h = 9 seconds, and sums of such values are too.

Keep format_hours (decimal notation) in the module. Do not delete it: it is still the right renderer for spreadsheet output. State in its docstring that it is for exports and raw-number contexts, not for screens.

Switch these call sites from format_hours to format_hours_human: apps/api/plane/app/serializers/service_log.py get_equivalent_hours_display (around line 257, the technician's 'o cliente ve ...' reading) and the client row serializer's get_equivalent_hours_display (around line 404); apps/api/plane/utils/service_portal.py issue_client_totals (around line 510, both equivalent_hours_display and debited_hours_display); apps/api/plane/utils/service_allowance.py the ledger entry hours_display (around line 987); apps/api/plane/utils/service_pool.py the period snapshot displays (around lines 1791-1809, including the parcel hours_display); apps/api/plane/utils/service_reports.py (around lines 227 and 820, the aggregate *_display builders). In each case only the *_display twin changes; the raw decimal string field beside it stays exactly as it is, because the frontend types document that the raw value is what callers compare and sort by.

Leave apps/api/plane/utils/exporters/schemas/service_log.py on format_hours and add a one-line comment saying why: CSV/XLSX rows are read by spreadsheets and invoicing, where a decimal is the useful form. This is the one deliberate exception and it must be visible in the code.

Add the missing display twins to the /preview response in apps/api/plane/app/views/service_log/base.py (the `totals` dict built around lines 509-518): logged_hours_display, equivalent_hours_display and debited_hours_display via format_hours_human, alongside the existing raw strings and the admin-only amount fields. Then extend the `totals` shape of IServiceLogPreview in packages/types/src/service-log.ts with the three new readonly display fields.

Fix the frontend consumers of those values: in apps/web/core/components/service-logs/service-log-form.tsx the split-preview total currently renders the raw string `preview.totals.logged_hours` ('1.2500') - render `preview.totals.logged_hours_display` instead; and in apps/web/core/store/issue/issue-details/service-log.store.ts change the EMPTY_TOTALS display seeds from '0h' to '0min' so an empty work item reads the same as one the server has answered for.

Grep the whole repo for any other place a raw hour string reaches the DOM (`grep -rn "totals\.\w*_hours[^_]" apps/web` and `grep -rn "_hours}" apps/web`) and fix any hit by switching it to the _display twin. Report what you found in findings even if the answer is nothing.

Update the tests that pin the old format: apps/api/plane/tests/contract/app/test_service_log_app.py lines around 735-736 and 753-754 assert equivalent_hours_display == '1,875h' - change the expectation to the new human string and keep the logged_hours_display assertion. Grep the whole test suite for other pinned decimal display strings (`grep -rn "h\"" apps/api/plane/tests | grep -i display` plus a search for the literal patterns '1,875h', '0,75h', ',25h') and update each. Do not weaken an assertion into a truthiness check: assert the exact new string, because a display test that only asserts 'something is there' is the false-green the conventions document forbids.

Add unit tests in apps/api/plane/tests/unit/utils/test_service_log_time.py for the new non-whole-minute behaviour: 1.8750 -> '1h 52min 30s', 0.3750 -> '22min 30s', a negative fractional value, and a value whose seconds are zero to prove no empty '0s' tail is emitted. Add a contract-level assertion that the /preview response carries logged_hours_display (in the existing preview test in test_service_log_app.py) and that the client work item totals no longer contain a comma-decimal hour string (assert the exact expected human string, not merely the absence of a comma).

Add an entry to docs/worklog/DECISOES.md as the next free decision number (D68 at the time of writing - check the file for the highest existing number) recording that every hour quantity on screen now reads as a clock duration, that format_hours survives for exports, that seconds appear only when the value is not whole-minute aligned, and that this refines R3's example ('1,25h quando o contexto exigir o numero') rather than contradicting the rule. Keep it in the same voice and structure as the surrounding decisions and in Portuguese, like the rest of that file.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn "format_hours(" apps/api/plane returns hits only in apps/api/plane/utils/service_log_time.py (definition and docstring references), apps/api/plane/utils/exporters/schemas/service_log.py, and tests - no serializer, view, portal, allowance, pool or reports module still renders a decimal hour for a screen.
format_hours_human(Decimal('1.8750')) == '1h 52min 30s' and format_hours_human(Decimal('1.2500')) == '1h 15min', with every pre-existing TestFormatHoursHuman assertion still passing unmodified.

The /preview response contains logged_hours_display, equivalent_hours_display and debited_hours_display, IServiceLogPreview declares them, and the split-preview line in service-log-form.tsx renders the display twin instead of the raw decimal.
No client-facing payload gained a field: the client serializer and issue_client_totals still expose exactly the same field names as before the change (only their *_display values changed).
`./tools/agent-sandbox/run-api-tests.sh -m unit` and the three worklog contract test files pass, with no assertion softened to a truthiness check.
`ruff check apps/api` passes and `./tools/agent-sandbox/run-web-checks.sh types` passes.
docs/worklog/DECISOES.md carries the new decision entry.
findings:
COMMIT 169168ec0 on fix/worklog-horas-legiveis-e-responsivo. 24 files, all local checks green.

WHAT CHANGED (api)
1. service_log_time.py: format_hours_human now rounds to the whole SECOND (ROUND_HALF_UP on value*3600) instead of to the minute, and emits a third term when a remainder exists: 1.8750 -> '1h 52min 30s', 0.3750 -> '22min 30s', 0.0025 -> '9s' (never '0min 9s'). Whole-minute output is byte-identical to before, so every pre-existing TestFormatHoursHuman assertion passes unmodified. Added named constants SECONDS_PER_MINUTE / SECONDS_PER_HOUR. format_hours kept, with a docstring saying it is for exports and raw-number contexts only.
2. Switched to format_hours_human: serializers/service_log.py get_equivalent_hours_display (both the technician serializer ~line 257 and the client row serializer ~line 404, each with a docstring saying why); service_portal.py issue_client_totals (equivalent + debited display); service_allowance.py allowance_credits hours_display; service_pool.py contract_balance_statement (all 7 period displays + the parcel hours_display); service_reports.py bucket() and headline_totals().
3. exporters/schemas/service_log.py left on format_hours with a 4-line comment saying why (spreadsheet + invoicing want a summable decimal) and telling the next reader not to 'finish the migration'. It is now the ONLY non-test caller of format_hours.
4. views/service_log/base.py /preview: totals gained logged_hours_display, equivalent_hours_display and debited_hours_display beside the existing raw strings; the two sums were hoisted into locals. Also dropped the unused format_hours from the import (resolved one of FEAT-001's two F401s).
5. serializers/service_issue_allowance.py: dropped the unused format_hours import (the other F401). ruff went from 18 pre-existing errors to 16; the remaining 16 are exactly FEAT-001's list minus those two, untouched on purpose.

GREP FOR RAW HOUR STRINGS REACHING THE DOM - the answer was NOT nothing. Six hits, all fixed by adding the _display twin in the API (never by formatting in the browser, which would be a second implementation of R3):
a. service-logs/service-log-form.tsx:321 rendered preview.totals.logged_hours ('1.2500') -> now logged_hours_display. This is the one the plan named.
b. service-pricing/overage-billing-confirmation.tsx:133 rendered preview.overage_hours -> added overage_hours_display to BOTH previews that feed that modal (service_pool.overage_billing_preview and service_allowance.allowance_overage_preview) and to IServiceOveragePreview.
c+d. service-reports/attention-tab.tsx:118 and :131 printed entry.balance_hours ('-2.0000') in the alert subtitle -> added balance_hours_display to both alert entry builders in service_pool_alerts.py (~line 532 period, ~line 712 allowance) and to TServicePeriodAlertEntry / TServiceAllowanceAlertEntry.
e. service-reports/billing-tab.tsx:111, :235, :256 concatenated a literal 'h' onto raw strings, printing '1.2500h' -> added hours_display to service_billing.py _render_consolidation (origins, commercial_pendencies, registration_pendencies, internal_work), updated the inline casts and TServiceBillingReport.internal_work.
f. service-reports/operational-tab.tsx:118 rendered totals.average_equivalent_hours_per_issue ('0.4286') -> added average_equivalent_hours_per_issue_display in headline_totals (the twin the money average already had) and render it with a '-' fallback since the field is optional (D53: no issues means no average, not zero). This is the only quantity in the feature that is NOT block-aligned, so it is the best example of why the seconds term exists.
Checked and deliberately left alone: charts.tsx / consumption-tab.tsx / portal-consumption-dashboard.tsx use Number(raw) only for chart values and conditional colour classes and render the _display twin as text (the file even carries the comment 'Raw to compare, _display to render'); service-log.helpers.ts formatHoursForInput builds the text for the duration INPUT, not a display; credit-service-allowance-modal value={hours} is a form field; issue_pool_snapshot's period dict has no display twins but nothing in apps/web renders it.

FRONTEND
- packages/types/src/service-log.ts: IServiceLogPreview.totals gained the three readonly display fields with a doc comment saying to render the twin.
- service-log.store.ts EMPTY_TOTALS displays '0h' -> '0min', matching what format_hours_human answers for zero, with a comment saying why.

TEST EXPECTATIONS UPDATED (every one asserts an exact string; nothing was softened)
- test_service_log_app.py::TestListingAndTotals::test_totals_carry_a_pt_br_rendering (FEAT-001's single baseline failure): logged_hours_display '1,25h' -> '1h 15min' and equivalent_hours_display '1,875h' -> '1h 52min 30s'. The endpoint was NOT reverted.
- test_service_log_app.py::test_the_row_carries_both_readings_of_r11: equivalent_hours_display '1,875h' -> '1h 52min 30s'.
- test_service_log_client_app.py::test_the_client_does_receive_the_hours_they_are_entitled_to: the truthiness check `assert row['equivalent_hours_display']` was STRENGTHENED to == '1h 30min' and a new assertion pins totals equivalent_hours_display == '3h'.
- No other pinned decimal display string existed anywhere in the suite: grep for hours_display, for '_display"] ==', and for the literals '1,875h' / '0,75h' / ',25h' found only the above plus the TestFormatHours unit tests, which are format_hours's own tests and must keep the decimal expectations.

TESTS ADDED
- unit/utils/test_service_log_time.py: test_a_value_that_is_not_whole_minutes_gains_a_seconds_term (1.8750, 0.3750, 0.0025, and two negative fractional values), test_a_whole_minute_value_emits_no_seconds_tail (four values, proving no '0s' tail), test_a_sub_second_remainder_rounds_to_the_nearest_second (0.00013 -> '0min', 0.0004 -> '1s').
- contract/app/test_service_log_app.py: test_the_preview_totals_carry_a_rendered_twin (all three twins plus the raw string beside them) and test_the_preview_renders_a_half_minute_equivalent_as_seconds (1.25h at multiplier 1.5 -> '1h 52min 30s', the exact case the user reported as '1,875h').

R11 CHECK: no client-facing payload gained a field. ServiceLogClientSerializer.Meta.fields and issue_client_totals expose exactly the same names as before; only the *_display VALUES changed. The existing structural test test_the_hidden_fields_are_not_merely_stripped_but_undeclared and the whole TestR11 class still pass.

DOCS: docs/worklog/DECISOES.md gained D68 (Portuguese, same voice and 'Resumo do que muda no codigo' table as the surrounding entries): every hour on screen is a clock duration, format_hours survives for exports, seconds appear only when the value is not whole-minute aligned, and this REFINES R3's '1,25h quando o contexto exigir o numero' by naming the export as that context rather than contradicting the rule. D67 was the previous highest number.

NOTE FOR FEAT-003: the husky pre-commit hook runs oxfmt on staged files and it REFORMATTED overage-billing-confirmation.tsx (Tailwind class ORDER inside className strings, e.g. 'rounded-full bg-red-500/15' -> 'bg-red-500/15 ... rounded-full', plus some line joins) and lightly touched the two types files. Cosmetic and already in the commit, but expect the same on any file you stage, and re-run types/lint after committing rather than only before. The reformat is why the commit diff for that file is larger than the one-line change I made.
Also relevant to FEAT-003: no string in the worklog UI is now longer than before EXCEPT the equivalent-hours reading, which can be '1h 52min 30s' (12 chars) where it used to be '1,875h' (6). The totals cards and the allowance figures must survive that at 390px, which is exactly the break-words / min-w-0 work FEAT-003 owns.
